# conpyro

<!-- badges: start -->

![lifecycle](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-beta-orange) ![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-GPL--3-blue)

<!-- badges: end -->

**Conifer Pyrometrics (ConPyro) fire behaviour modelling tools for R**

## Overview

`conpyro` is an R package implementing the **Conifer Pyrometrics (ConPyro)**
fire behaviour modelling system introduced by Perrakis et al. (2020).
Subsequent developments include crown fire occurrence models
(Perrakis et al., 2023) and surface fire spread models
(Perrakis et al., 2026). See [References](#references) below.

> **Prefer a graphical interface?**
>
> [FuelDash](https://pfcfire.shinyapps.io/FuelDash/) provides a user-friendly
> web interface to conpyro, with interactive calculators and plots for
> exploring fire behaviour without writing R code.

This package provides tools for estimating:

-   Stand-adjusted and FFMC-based fine fuel moisture content
-   Crown fire occurrence probability
-   Passive and active crown fire wind speed thresholds
-   Surface and crown fire rate of spread

It is designed for both **single-scenario exploratory modelling**, and **large multi-scenario workflows**, including modeling driven by spatial datasets, allowing users to evaluate fire behaviour across many fuel and fire weather configurations.

This GitHub release is a **beta version intended for testing and feedback prior to CRAN submission.**

**Note:** Both this software and the underlying ConPyro models are still under active development. Model outputs are estimates intended for informational and exploratory purposes only and should not be interpreted as definitive
predictions of fire behaviour.

## Installation & Dependencies

Install the **beta version** from GitHub:

```{r eval=FALSE}
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("nhebda/conpyro")
```

Some optional helper functions rely on the package `cffdrs`. If you plan to use those tools, install it separately:

```{r eval=FALSE}
install.packages("cffdrs")
```

Optional plotting of results requires `ggplot2`:

```{r eval=FALSE}
install.packages("ggplot2")
```

## Basic Example

The main modelling function is `conpyro()`, which calculates crown fire occurrence probability, crowning thresholds, and rate of spread across a vector of 10-m open wind speeds.

```{r eval=FALSE}
library(conpyro)

conpyro(
  data = default_input,
  WS10 = 0:40,
  FFMC = 91,
  DMC = 85
)
```

This calculates fire behaviour metrics for each scenario defined in `data`
across wind speeds from **0–40 km/h**.

## Input Methods

Inputs can be supplied in two ways:

### 1. Data frame input (recommended for many scenarios)

Each row in `data` represents a scenario: a single fuel and fire weather
configuration. The example below assumes `my_scenarios` contains the required
`FFMC`, `FSG`, `SFC`, and `CBD` columns, plus any optional scenario inputs.
Wind speeds are supplied separately and shared across scenarios.

```{r eval=FALSE}
conpyro(
  data = my_scenarios,
  WS10 = 0:30
)
```

### 2. Direct arguments

Inputs may also be supplied directly as arguments, with length `1` or the
**common number of scenarios**.

```{r eval=FALSE}
conpyro(
  WS10 = 0:40,
  FFMC = c(89, 91, 92),
  FSG = 6,
  SFC = 2,
  CBD = 0.1,
  DMC = c(23, 50, 80),
  season = c("spring", "summer", "summer"),
  density = "moderate",
  stand = "pine"
)
```

Length `1` scenario inputs are recycled across all scenarios. `WS10` is a
shared wind-speed vector, rather than a scenario input. Data-frame columns
and direct arguments can be combined, provided the same input is not
supplied through both methods.

## Moisture and Model Selection

`conpyro()` calculates stand-adjusted moisture (`mcsa`) when `DMC`, `season`,
`density`, and `stand` are all available for a scenario. Otherwise, it uses
FFMC-based moisture (`mcF`).

Default crown fire occurrence and surface ROS models follow that moisture
selection:

| Moisture | `model_pCFO` | `model_sROS` |
|---|---:|---:|
| FFMC-based (`mcF`) | 10 | 12 |
| Stand-adjusted (`mcsa`) | 11 | 13 |

Advanced users can select alternative models through arguments such as
`model_pCFO`, `model_sROS`, and `model_cROS`.

Model overrides do not enforce compatibility with the selected moisture or
fuel type. Consult the function documentation and relevant papers before
choosing alternatives:

```{r eval=FALSE}
help("conpyro", package = "conpyro")
help("t_ROS", package = "conpyro")
```

Crowning thresholds are the lowest supplied wind speeds classified in each
crown-fire regime. Their resolution depends on the spacing of values in the
supplied wind-speed vector; `NA` means that regime was absent from those
values.

## Plotting Results

`conpyro()` can optionally generate plots of model outputs.

```{r eval=FALSE}
conpyro(
  data = default_input,
  WS10 = 0:40,
  FFMC = 91,
  DMC = 85,
  plot = c("pCFO", "ROS")
)
```

Available plot types:

-   `"pCFO"` – Crown fire occurrence probability
-   `"CAC"` – Criterion for active crowning
-   `"ROS"` – Composite rate-of-spread plot with crowning thresholds

Plotting requires **ggplot2**.

## Helper Tools

The package includes a number of helper functions for calculating model inputs and intermediate quantities for single scenarios.

### Fine fuel moisture estimation

-   `t_mcF()` – FFMC-based fine fuel moisture content
-   `t_mcsa()` – Stand-adjusted fine fuel moisture
-   `t_mcSeason()` – Season category from month and day
-   `t_mcDensity()` – Density category from canopy closure

### Fire modelling

-   `t_pCFO()` – Crown fire occurrence probability
-   `t_FT()` – Fire type classification
-   `t_ROS()` – Equilibrium rate of spread

### Surface fuel consumption

-   `t_SFC_FBP()` – FBPS-based SFC
-   `t_SFC_deGroot()` – De Groot et al. (2009) SFC equation

### Foliar moisture

-   `t_FMC()` – Foliar moisture content estimate

### Experimental ladder fuel tools

-   `ladder_standing_dead()`
-   `ladder_midstory_saplings()`

These tools allow users to explore individual components of the ConPyro modeling system.

## Beta Status

This package is currently in **beta testing**.

During this phase we aim to:

-   Collect feedback from fire behaviour researchers and practitioners
-   Identify edge cases and bugs
-   Refine documentation and usability
-   Evaluate performance for large-scale modelling workflows

The package interface may evolve prior to a future CRAN release.

## References

**Modelling framework**

Perrakis, D. D. B., Cruz, M. G., Alexander, M. E., Taylor, S. W., and
Beverly, J. L. (2020). Linking Dynamic Empirical Fire Spread Models:
Introducing Canadian Conifer Pyrometrics. In *Proceedings for the 6th
International Fire Behavior and Fuels Conference*, pp. 67–72.
International Association of Wildland Fire.
[Conference paper][conpyro-framework].

**Crown fire occurrence**

Perrakis, D. D. B., Cruz, M. G., Alexander, M. E., Hanes, C. C.,
Thompson, D. K., Taylor, S. W., and Stocks, B. J. (2023).
Improved logistic models of crown fire probability in Canadian conifer
forests. *International Journal of Wildland Fire*, 32(10), 1455–1473.
<https://doi.org/10.1071/WF23074>

**Surface fire spread**

Perrakis, D. D. B., Hebda, N. J. R., and Taylor, S. W. (2026).
Simple Spread Models for Understory Surface Fires.
*Fire*, 9(7), 302.
<https://doi.org/10.3390/fire9070302>

The system also incorporates FWI moisture relationships and selected FBP
equations, alongside stand-adjusted fuel moisture and crown fire spread
models from other sources. See the function documentation and these papers
for further attribution.

[conpyro-framework]: https://fireresearch.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/perrakis-et-al-2020-linking-dynamic-empirical-spread-models-conpyro-proc-6th-int-fire-b-and-fuels.pdf
